canvas.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "canvas and playground container" — narrower than the prior "page/app background" meaning, now specifically the live-preview/demo container surface. Value moved off neutral.white (was briefly byte-identical to bg.surface/bg.subtle) to gray.100, one step past bg.subtle (gray.50), so it reads as a visually distinct container again. Contrast re-verified: text.primary 12.41:1, text.secondary 6.05:1 — both clear AA. Byte-identical to border.subtle (also gray.100) — nothing currently pairs the two, flagged here in case a future component draws a border.subtle border directly on bg.canvas.

surface.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "page, card, sheet and drawer background" — broadens from "card/panel surface" to cover every default content surface, not just cards. Value unchanged (white).

surface-raised.$description: Usage description added (2026-08-08): "an elevated surface (paired with a shadow)". Value unchanged (white, byte-identical to bg.surface in light mode — elevation here comes from the paired shadow, not a background difference).

subtle.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "hover fill for tertiary/ghost controls, dashboard panel, neutral accent" — broadens from hover-fill/zebra-striping to also cover dashboard panels and general neutral accents. Value unchanged (gray.50). History: swapped with canvas 2026-07-27, when subtle was defined as the barely-visible tint layered on top of white bg.surface.

brand-subtle.$description: Moved from purple.100 to purple.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction (matching bg.info-subtle's earlier move). Dark theme moved correspondingly (purple.900 → purple.950). Real consumers re-verified: Avatar's text.link (purple.600) on purple.50 = 7.03:1 (was 6.47:1 on purple.100); ListItem's selected state (text.primary, gray.900) on purple.50 = 13.46:1 — both still comfortably pass AA.

brand-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state (a subtle-background fill darkening one step on hover, the same direction bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover already use for their own solid fills). purple.100 is brand-subtle's own value before its 2026-07-27 move to purple.50, so this reuses an already-generated scale step rather than needing a new one. text.link (purple.600) on purple.100 = 6.47:1, comfortably passes AA.

danger-subtle.$description: Moved from red.100 to red.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (red.900 → red.950). text.danger (red.700) on red.50 = 7.05:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 6.43:1 on red.100).

danger-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses danger-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (red.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.danger (red.700) on red.100 = 6.43:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching danger-subtle's own brand-independence.

warning-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.warning, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-warning on amber.700 = 6.96:1, passes AA.

warning-subtle.$description: Moved from amber.100 to amber.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (amber.900 → amber.950). text.warning (amber.800) on amber.50 = 9.74:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.90:1 on amber.100).

warning-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses warning-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (amber.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.warning (amber.800) on amber.100 = 8.90:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching warning-subtle's own brand-independence.

success.$description: Solid fill hosting text.on-success. green.600 (pre-OKLCH-regen step) gave neither white nor gray.950 text 4.5:1 (4.39:1 / 4.13:1) — green.700 gives white text 6.50:1 (verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4).

success-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.success, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-success on green.800 = 9.56:1, passes AA.

success-subtle.$description: Moved from green.100 to green.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (green.900 → green.950). text.success (green.800) on green.50 = 9.15:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.42:1 on green.100).

success-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses success-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (green.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.success (green.800) on green.100 = 8.42:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching success-subtle's own brand-independence.

info-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.info, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-info on blue.700 = 6.93:1, passes AA.

info-subtle.$description: Moved from blue.100 to blue.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (blue.900 → blue.950, the mirror-opposite extreme) to preserve the same relative gap. text.info (blue.700) on blue.50 = 6.63:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 6.10:1 on blue.100).

info-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses info-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (blue.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.info (blue.700) on blue.100 = 6.10:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching info-subtle's own brand-independence.

neutral.$description: Fifth status-tone fill, for neutral/offline-style indicators (e.g. Avatar's offline status dot). gray.500 on bg.surface: 3.25:1 light / 4.34:1 dark, both pass WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1) — re-verified 2026-07-18 (Phase 4, OKLCH regen), shared across all 4 themes since gray.500 uniquely satisfies both.

neutral-strong.$description: Solid neutral fill for hosting text (Badge's solid variant, neutral tone) — bg.neutral (gray.500) is only verified for the 3:1 non-text case. gray.600 with white text gives 4.70:1, passing everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

overlay.$description: Dimming scrim behind Dialog/Drawer/overlays (Backdrop atom). No text sits directly on it, so it isn't a WCAG contrast pairing — opacity is applied separately, compositionally, via the opacity.* scale rather than baked into this token, matching how color and opacity stay separate token categories everywhere else. Shared across all 4 themes since dimming what's behind isn't a brand-dependent decision.

code.$description: New token (2026-08-08) for inline code/token-reference pills in Storybook documentation (docs.css's .dbm-tokentable code) — mirrors bg.info-subtle's exact blue.50/blue.950 lightness-curve values, but under a name that doesn't imply status/info meaning, since a plain code reference isn't a status. Not currently consumed by any published component (the real Code.tsx atom uses bg.subtle instead) — Storybook-docs-only for now.

tertiary.$description: gray.500 fails AA (needs 4.5:1) for this token's literal-text uses (Text color="tertiary", Divider label, Input placeholder). gray.600 gives 4.70:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen), still lighter/more muted than text.secondary (gray.700).

on-danger.$description: Text on a solid bg.danger fill. White on red.600 = 5.10:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use gray.950 instead — see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json.

on-info.$description: Text on a solid bg.info fill (Badge solid variant). White on blue.600 = 4.71:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use gray.950 instead — see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json.

on-success.$description: Text on a solid bg.success fill (Badge solid variant). Post-OKLCH-regen (Phase 4, 2026-07-18): light-theme bg.success is green.700, where white gives 6.50:1. Dark theme keeps gray.950 against green.500 (5.91:1) — white fails there (3.07:1) — so this token is now theme-specific rather than shared; see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json.

on-warning.$description: Text on a solid bg.warning fill (Badge solid variant). Post-OKLCH-regen (Phase 4, 2026-07-18): light-theme bg.warning (amber.600) gives white 4.78:1. Dark theme keeps gray.950 against amber.500 (5.49:1) — white fails there (3.31:1) — so this token is now theme-specific; see purple-dark.json / emerald-dark.json.

on-neutral.$description: Text on a solid bg.neutral-strong fill (Badge solid variant). White on gray.600 = 4.70:1, passes everywhere — shared across all 4 themes (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen).

brand.$description: Accent text drawn from the brand color (2026-07-27) — for emphasis/labels, not links (see text.link). Reuses the same resolved value as text.link since both need an AA-safe brand-colored text color on bg.surface: purple.600 on white = 7.37:1. NOT a literal 'primitive step 600 in every theme' constant — emerald-light/both dark themes use a different step for the same reason text.link does (see emerald-light.json / *-dark.json).

success.$description: green.800 on bg.success-subtle (green.100) gives 8.42:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen — originally fixed in Phase 3 when the HSL-derived scales gave green.700 only 4.08:1, failing AA).

brand.$description: Brand-accent border, decorative-only (2026-07-27, revised from purple.500). purple.100 on white is only 1.14:1, well below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor — deliberately accepted, since this token is for decorative UI accents rather than a border that identifies a component/state boundary (which is what 1.4.11 actually governs; border.focus/border.danger remain contrast-verified since those ARE state-identifying). No longer literal across every theme as of 2026-08-16 — dark mode moved to purple.900 (see that file's own description) so each mode gets its own similarly-subtle contrast ratio instead of sharing one literal value that read very differently against each mode's background.

code.$description: Paired with bg.code (2026-08-08) — blue.100/blue.900, a purely decorative border, not one that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply — same accepted class as border.brand. Measures 1.09:1 light / 1.28:1 dark against bg.code, an accepted tradeoff, not an oversight.

secondary.$description: gray.400 on bg.surface was 2.32:1, failing the WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor (3:1) — found during the Phase 4 icon-contrast sweep (2026-07-18) while this token was still unused by any shipped component. gray.500 gives 3.25:1, and stays more muted than icon.default (gray.600, 4.70:1).
